I don’t have the ability to make live calls to the VirusTotal service from here, but I can show you exactly what you’d need to run locally (or in your own environment) to pull those first 25 resolution records. --- ### Quick‑start: Using the official `virustotal-python` library ```bash pip install virustotal-api ``` ```python from virustotal_python import Virustotal import json API_KEY = "sec_key5" IP_ADDRESS = "67.89.0.1" vt = Virustotal(API_KEY) # Get the IP object – this returns all available data for that IP response = vt.get_ip(IP_ADDRESS) if response.status_code == 200: ip_data = response.json() else: print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}") exit(1) # The “resolutions” field contains the historical DNS resolution data resolutions = ip_data.get("data", {}).get("attributes", {}).get("resolutions", []) print(f"Found {len(resolutions)} total resolution entries.") for entry in resolutions[:25]: # Grab only the first 25 resolved_at = entry["resolved_at"] hostname = entry["hostname"] print(f"{resolved_at}\t{hostname}") # If you want to write them out to a file: with open("ip_resolutions.txt", "w") as f: for entry in resolutions[:25]: f.write(f"{entry['resolved_at']}\t{entry['hostname']}\n") ``` **What this does** | Step | What happens | |------|--------------| | `vt.get_ip(IP_ADDRESS)` | Calls `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/67.89.0.1`. | | `.json()` | Parses the JSON payload returned by VT. | | `...get("resolutions", [])` | Pulls the array under `data.attributes.resolutions`. | | `resolutions[:25]` | Slices the list to keep only the first 25 items. | --- ### Alternative: Raw HTTP request (no library) If you prefer not to install the wrapper: ```python import requests import json API_KEY = "sec_key5" IP_ADDRESS = "67.89.0.1" URL = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{IP_ADDRESS}" headers = { "x-apikey": API_KEY, } resp = requests.get(URL, headers=headers) if resp.status_code != 200: raise RuntimeError(f"Request failed ({resp.status_code}): {resp.text}") ip_json = resp.json() resolutions = ip_json.get("data", {}).get("attributes", {}).get("resolutions", []) print(f"Total resolutions found: {len(resolutions)}") for res in resolutions[:25]: print(f"{res['resolved_at']} -> {res['hostname']}") ``` --- ### Things to keep in mind | Item | Why it matters | |------|----------------| | **Rate limits** | VirusTotal’s free tier allows ~4 requests/minute. If you’re pulling many IPs, add a short sleep (`time.sleep(15)`) between calls. | | **Pagination** | For most IP queries the entire dataset comes back in one shot; however, if you hit a very busy IP you might see a `pagination` object. In that case you’ll need to follow the `next` link until you’ve collected enough records. | | **Data fields** | Each resolution record looks like:
`{"hostname":"example.com","resolved_at":"2022‑01‑12T14:23:00Z","ipv4_address":"192.0.2.123"}`
Feel free to adjust the output formatting to match your downstream needs. | --- #### TL;DR Run the snippet above with your API key (`sec_key5`) and it will fetch the full resolution history for `67.89.0.1`, then print (and optionally save) the first 25 entries.
